The core answer (right operand is not evaluated) is correct, but both code examples are backwards. In `ptr != NULL || *ptr == 0`, a NULL ptr makes the left side false, so `*ptr` IS evaluated (null dereference). Same for `i < n || a[i] == key` when i >= n (out-of-bounds read). The comments claiming the right side is skipped are wrong, and a correct guard needs the opposite test (e.g. `ptr == NULL || ...`). Notable error, so 3 in Accuracy.
